review_method: Read frozen adapter, runner, manifest, scripts and CLI/parser source; no CLI execution or physical assay performed by this review
scope_limits: Every source record states procedure_provided=false. Frozen amounts, order, solvent, boundary, activation and elapsed time are declared screening assumptions, not source-validated procedures.

Execution success is not a scientific pass. Negative outcomes require review of identity admission, procedure compatibility, model boundaries and observation coverage before attributing a chemistry defect.
The CLI exits at the first failed command in each script. Attempting all 200 scripts does not establish that every reactant, activation or final inspection was reached.

The outer runner continues after individual nonzero exits and timeouts, but a resource-gate stop leaves later records unexecuted. Any continuation must identify unfinished records and preserve completed evidence.

Added ingredients use registry phases; dataset phase labels cannot override them. Symbolic coefficients normalized to one are finite contact probes, not polymer stoichiometry or molecular-weight validation.
Sealed headspaces include initial air. Oxygen, nitrogen and carbon dioxide already present must be distinguished from reaction products; initial oxygen can also introduce a reagent.

Catalysts, auxiliary reagents, electrode systems and multistage work-ups absent from the frozen setup are not implicitly supplied by the CLI. A short wait does not establish a predicted reaction rate.

water_setup_review.adapter_rule: Add 100 mL water if any reactant OR product has an aqueous phase label
water_setup_review.reason_for_followup: An aqueous product label alone does not establish a compatible reaction medium. The listed organic probes have incomplete conditions, and bulk water can quench reactive species or change the intended pathway.

cases_requiring_reviewed_followup.source_condition: Alkoxide and a suitable primary alkyl halide.
cases_requiring_reviewed_followup.limitation: Added bulk water introduces proton transfer and competing aqueous substitution; the source does not specify this solvent or an alkoxide-compatible medium.
Base identity, concentration and medium determine elimination versus substitution. The added water is a screening assumption and does not establish the stated elimination-favouring conditions.
Bulk water can protonate the acetylide. The frozen aqueous contact does not establish a compatible alkylation protocol.

cases_requiring_reviewed_followup.source_condition: Conditions favouring C- rather than O-alkylation.
cases_requiring_reviewed_followup.limitation: Water can protonate the enolate and changes competing pathways; the frozen setup does not establish the required selectivity conditions.

The named palladium catalyst/ligand system and base conditions are not supplied. Added water is unvalidated for this example; aqueous variants existing in principle would not validate this catalyst-free contact probe.

starch_identity_review.finding: The adapter labels starch unresolved because the source leaves formula and charge unspecified, then submits the original starch token. That token is an admitted registry identity using C6H10O5 repeat-unit composition.
starch_identity_review.quantity_interpretation: The submitted 0.001 mol is a registry repeat-unit surrogate, not a measured quantity of polymer molecules or a defined chain-length distribution.
limits: An unresolved mapping label does not guarantee a CLI unknown-identity refusal.
Successful admission does not validate polymer molecular weight, chain count or quantitative hydrolysis yield.

preservation: This sidecar annotates interpretation only. Frozen forecasts, scripts, adapter, runner, bindings and the already dispatched execution remain unchanged.
